subject: Drift detection — rapid response playbook and canary rollback triggers
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Drift detection — rapid response playbook and canary rollback triggers

Team,

We observed an uptick in prompt-set X failures in yesterday's A/B that looks like a quality drift (higher hallucination rate and more incomplete answers). Numbers are modest but trending for two consecutive cohorts, and Acme flagged a few customer-facing regressions. I drafted a short "rapid response" playbook and a minimal canary rollback trigger so we have clear, aligned steps next time a signal appears. Draft attached: drift_playbook_draft.md.

What I need from each of you in this thread:
- Product (Marissa): finalize acceptance criteria we gate on (metric names, thresholds, cohort windows).
- Evals/Quality (Evelyn): confirm the diagnostic checks (synthetic prompt slices, hallucination classifier) and recommended sample sizes for signal confidence.
- Observability/Runtime (Aditya): list the metric queries and canary config we'd push to infra (attachment canary_config.yaml).
- Leadership (Grace): quick approvals and decision authority for a fast rollback if threshold hit.

Initial proposal (TL;DR):
- Trigger = any cohort where absolute hallucination rate increases >= 2.5pp and win-rate delta <= -3.0pp vs baseline for two consecutive cohorts (48 hour window).
- Immediate action = pause rollout to 100% and switch traffic to pinned model variant; kick off triage with owners and block releases until post-mortem.
- Communication = notify customer contacts (Acme support) within 60 minutes if customer-affecting examples present.

Attach: drift_playbook_draft.md (playbook + checklist), canary_config.yaml (suggested circuit-breaker thresholds).

I can host a 30-min sync tomorrow to move to an actionable MAP (mutual action plan).

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product — Evals & Quality

On Tue, May 28, 2029 at 10:12 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team,

> We observed an uptick in prompt-set X failures in yesterday's A/B...

Thanks for the clear draft, Karthik. High level I agree with the approach — want to tighten a couple of product-level asks so the playbook is actionable for PM/eng during a hot fix:

- Acceptance metrics (product):
  - Primary: user-facing win-rate (model preference in A/B) — rollback if absolute drop >= 3.0 percentage points over baseline in two consecutive cohorts.
  - Secondary: hallucination rate (measured by our hallucination classifier) — rollback if increase >= 2.5 percentage points and validated by a 50-sample manual spot check showing >= 15% confirmed hallucinations.
  - Tertiary: latency 95/99 degradation > 30% for 2+ minutes during canary traffic.

- Cohort definition: 6-hour rolling cohorts for canaries, 24-hour for wider rollout checks.
- A/B plan: preserve current sampling buckets and ensure canary gets at least 2% of live traffic for 2 consecutive cohorts before scaling. If signal appears, stop scaling and run expanded evaluation on the same promptset slices used for acceptance.

I can own the product-side acceptance doc and add a short checklist for CS comms to Acme. Can we make the manual spot-check step explicit in the playbook (owner: Marissa)?

Marissa
Senior PM — Models

Date: Wed, 29 May 2029 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Drift detection — rapid response playbook and canary rollback triggers

On Tue, May 28, 2029 at 11:05 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the clear draft, Karthik...

Adding the eval/quality perspective:

- Diagnostic checks to include in playbook:
  - Synthetic slice run: run our standard 1k synthetic seeds across prompt-set X and measure consistency with baseline (M1).
  - Hallucination classifier + adjudication: run classifier, then 50-sample manual adjudication for high-confidence anomalies.
  - Output distribution drift: KL divergence on token distributions and categorical output labels we track.

- Sample sizes: canary-level (2% traffic) should give ~200 requests / 6-hour cohort for most customers; to reach confidence threshold we need at least 400 examples across two cohorts — if we don't have that, escalate to targeted sampling (force-sample).

- A/B acceptance: require both automated metric signal AND manual adjudication where applicable before declaring a regression. If automated signal alone, label as "investigate" and throttle scaling until adjudicated.

I'll update the playbook with concrete diagnostic queries and a short adjudication form (who, what counts as hallucination, examples). Putting draft sections into drift_playbook_draft.md now.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Drift detection — rapid response playbook and canary rollback triggers

On Wed, May 29, 2029 at 09:30 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Adding the eval/quality perspective: ...

I pushed a suggested canary_config.yaml with pragmatic thresholds and the metric queries we should ship into the monitoring tier (attached). Highlights:

- Queries:
  - hallucination_rate: SUM(hallucination_flag) / COUNT(*) by cohort (6h and 24h windows)
  - win_rate_delta: compare model.variant.win_rate vs baseline variant over 2 rolling cohorts
  - kl_token_divergence: compute on 1k-sample rolling window

- Circuit-breaker logic (canary_config.yaml):
  - If hallucination_rate change >= 2.5pp AND win_rate_delta <= -3pp for two consecutive 6h cohorts => set canary.break = true and route 100% of traffic to pinned variant.
  - Send automated Slack + email to triage channel and owners; include pre-baked link to adjudication form.

Operational notes:
- Force-sampling (if not enough examples) can be toggled via runtime flag: runtime.force_sample.promptset_x = true (requires engineering sign-off but fast).
- I'm including a short Grafana dashboard snippet link in the drive folder for triage.

Attachment: canary_config.yaml (in thread attachments).

Aditya
Staff SW Eng — Runtime + Observability
Redwood Inference

2) Customer comms: if Acme sees customer-facing examples we notify their security@ and account team within 60 minutes. Grace/CS to approve the templated blurb — Marissa to prepare.
3) Legal: cc'd legal for any potential compliance blips (we'll route through legal@redwood.ai).
4) Training: schedule a 30-min tabletop for triage owners next week (I can host).

Please confirm owners and I will mark playbook as approved for rollout to staging.
